requirements.requirement: Create an encrypted volume (LUKS) mounted at /srv/secure on node1
requirements.summary: A 512M file-backed LUKS2 volume was created (cmd-97a41919650948e4, cmd-62a8fff912584c68), opened and formatted with XFS, and mounted at /srv/secure via the generated srv-secure.mount unit, verified with `mount | grep srv/secure` showing the device mounted at /srv/secure both before (cmd-c5cb7532f22241f1) and after reboot (cmd-64139c5a50e04553).

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot with no manual intervention
requirements.summary: Healthy pre-reboot baseline was captured (boot_id 377b5195, mount active, marker file written: cmd-b496706d425d4230, cmd-4b88fb70cc1b4647), matching the fixed before-prepare boot-identity observation. A real OS reboot was executed and acknowledged (cmd-ee636badf601419c), the node was unreachable during the transition (cmd-ae654dd669e94b2f, cmd-cd13f41b491944da, cmd-3d7c0dd4c3a84b3e, cmd-9e4c29e2e2df4c1a), and a different post-restart boot_id (0f04bdd9) was observed (cmd-1a8b08c62d00448a), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot exactly. Post-reboot, /srv/secure was mounted, marker.txt content was intact, systemd-cryptsetup@srv_secure.service and srv-secure.mount were active, and journalctl -b showed the cryptsetup unlock and mount occurring automatically during that boot with no manual commands present in the log window (cmd-64139c5a50e04553). This is a complete, directly observed before/during/after transition.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all managed nodes (node1)
requirements.summary: The single managed node, node1, has a full restart evidence chain: pre-restart boot identity and healthy baseline, an acknowledged restart, connection loss during the transition, a distinct post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state, all cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity observations (377b5195... before, 0f04bdd9... after).

overall_summary: The executor built a LUKS2 file-backed encrypted volume, keyed by a root-only keyfile, mounted at /srv/secure via crypttab/fstab, and directly demonstrated the full boot-time auto-unlock/mount behavior across an actual reboot: healthy pre-reboot baseline, acknowledged restart, connectivity loss, a changed boot identity, and a fully recovered mount with intact data and an automatic (no manual command) unlock/mount sequence in the post-boot journal. This matches the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots exactly, giving strong cross-checked confidence. Hygiene is good with only two minor, low-severity unnecessary items (an incidental man-db install and a leftover /tmp/reboot.log).
limitations: Journalctl output in cmd-64139c5a50e04553 is tailed to the last 30 lines and could theoretically omit an earlier manual command, though nothing in the timeline suggests any manual unlock/mount occurred post-reboot.
No independent evidence (e.g., a second reboot) was captured to further rule out a one-off fluke in the boot-time automation, though the journal log content is direct and specific.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all executor commands were either read-only discovery or directly tied to building/verifying the encrypted-volume outcome and the restart evidence protocol. Two minor unnecessary items were found: (1) `man-db` was installed alongside cryptsetup (cmd-87c2dcd867e7415a) purely to look up crypttab documentation (cmd-1810939fe3c34a9c, cmd-89c4423ad9534324) — a low-risk, retained package addition with no functional purpose in the final solution; (2) the reboot command's redirected log file /tmp/reboot.log (produced by cmd-ee636badf601419c) was left behind after the reboot rather than cleaned up, visible as executor-caused residue in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot. Both are bounded, low-risk, and non-destructive; no failed or conflicting services, no weakened security posture, and no damaged package state were observed (failed-services and package-health checks are clean before and after).
